planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; this large-flowered coneflower benefits from deep watering during its first season.

directions: Big Kahuna produces oversized, vividly colored daisy flowers on sturdy, well-branched stems, standing out in a border for sheer bloom size compared with older coneflower cultivars. It blooms through the heat of summer into fall and draws steady pollinator and bird traffic once seed heads form. Deadhead through summer to extend flowering, then leave the last flush of seed heads standing for finches over winter. Once rooted in it shrugs off dry spells and needs no routine feeding beyond an annual compost topdressing.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Moab Sunset opens warm orange-red petals that shift tone as each flower ages, giving a single clump a layered, sunset-like color range through the bloom season. Its compact, well-branched habit keeps the display dense without staking, and the long summer-into-fall bloom window makes it a reliable pollinator plant. Deadhead regularly for continued flowering or let late-season seed heads stand for birds. It tolerates heat and drought well once established and needs little beyond occasional deep watering in extended dry spells.

planting.note: Plant after last frost in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; established plants resent winter wet more than cold.

directions: Prince's Plume sends up tall, dense spikes of tubular flowers over aromatic foliage, a vertical accent that draws hummingbirds and bees from summer through fall. It needs sharp drainage above all else, since wet winter soil is far more likely to kill it than cold itself. Shear spent spikes to tidy the clump and encourage continued bloom through the season. Once established it tolerates heat and drought with only occasional supplemental water.

planting.note: Plant in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Desert Coral opens coral-pink daisy flowers over a long summer season on a compact, self-branching mound. It tolerates heat and drought well once established and needs little beyond deadheading to keep new buds forming. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor. Avoid heavy, poorly drained soil, which shortens the plant's lifespan.

planting.note: Plant in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Imperial Sun carries rich golden-yellow flowers in heavy profusion over a tidy, compact mound, blooming from early summer well into fall. It handles heat and dry spells readily once rooted in and needs only occasional deadheading to sustain bloom. Divide every few years in spring if the clump's center begins to thin. Good drainage matters more than soil fertility for long-term vigor.

planting.note: Plant in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Ruby Frost shows deep ruby-red petals edged in a lighter frosted rim, a two-tone effect that stands out against the plant's fine, ferny foliage. It flowers heavily from early summer into fall on a compact mound well suited to border fronts and containers. Deadhead regularly to extend bloom, and divide every few years to keep plants vigorous. It tolerates heat and drought well but declines in soggy soil.

planting.note: Plant in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; good drainage over winter is essential.

directions: Lemon Popsicle sends up compact, bottlebrush-like flower spikes in clear lemon-yellow above grassy, arching foliage, blooming over a long stretch from late spring into summer. Its dwarf habit suits smaller borders and containers better than older, taller red hot poker cultivars. Give it sharp winter drainage, since wet, cold soil is the main threat to its survival. Deadhead spent spikes to tidy the clump and encourage repeat flowering.

common_name: Orange Vanilla Popsicle Red Hot Poker

planting.note: Plant in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; good drainage over winter is essential.

directions: Orange Vanilla Popsicle pairs a bright orange flower tip with a creamy vanilla-white base on each compact spike, giving the bicolor bottlebrush bloom extra visual depth. Flowering runs from late spring into summer on a dwarf, grassy-leaved clump well suited to containers and small borders. Winter drainage is critical, since cold, wet soil kills this selection faster than low temperature alone. Deadhead spent spikes to keep the clump tidy and encourage a longer bloom run.
